preamble: The shift from the voiced alveolar fricative [z] to the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ], triggered by a following palatal glide (English yod-coalescence of /zj/) or, in Portuguese, by coda position: the coda sibilant is postalveolar in Portugal and Rio de Janeiro, so voiced [z] before a voiced consonant appears as [ʒ].

examples.note: /zj/ coalesced to [ʒ] in words ending in vowel + -sure (also -sion).
Coalescence of /zj/ to [ʒ] also applies in stressed syllables for many speakers.
The coda sibilant is postalveolar in Portugal and Rio; before voiced consonants it is [ʒ] (also Islão [iʒˈlɐ̃w̃]).

Wikipedia describes Tayart and Tawellemmet as keeping *z as z but turning it into ž [ʒ] before the front vowel *i, hence the name Tamajaq; elsewhere z stays (Tawellemmet eɣăzăr 'valley'). Both dialects also palatalize dentals before /i/ and /j/.

sources: Wikipedia. Phonological history of English consonant clusters (Yod-coalescence). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_English_consonant_clusters
